notes.title: Documentation pilot — what it is actually like
notes.content:
Eight weeks in. The honest version.

When it works it saves me perhaps twenty minutes at the end of a shift. When it drops a note because the workstation timed out, it costs me more than it saved, and it does that roughly twice a week.

The suggestion timing is wrong. It offers before I have finished thinking, and the effort of dismissing something wrong is not zero — it is a small tax on every encounter.

notes.title: Rota — spring
notes.content:
Seven on, seven off. On weeks run 07:00 to 19:00 with handover either side.

During an on week I am not available for meetings and messages get answered in hours, not minutes. During an off week I am available and generally would rather not be.

notes.title: Feedback I gave the informaticist
notes.content:
Told Kenji verbally on the floor about the two-charts problem — the pane does not follow when I switch encounters. I have caught it every time so far.

I did not file a ticket because filing a ticket means writing down which patients were open, and I am not doing that.

notes.title: What I will not do
notes.content:
I have been asked twice by the pilot team for a real example so they can see the problem. The answer is no.

A de-identified example is also no. This is a two-unit pilot in a mid-size hospital; a colleague reading a de-identified case can place it in about four seconds.

notes.title: Handover protocol
notes.content: Verbal plus written at 07:00 and 19:00. Anything unresolved goes in writing with an owner. The pilot has not changed this and should not.

notes.title: Service structure — hospitalist
notes.content:
Seven on, seven off. On weeks: 07:00 handover, round, admissions through the day, 19:00 handover.

Average census fourteen to eighteen. Above eighteen the day stops being about medicine and starts being about triage.

notes.title: Handover — what actually transfers
notes.content:
Written plus verbal. The written part carries the plan; the verbal part carries the worry.

The worry is the bit that does not survive a written-only handover and it is the bit that matters at 2am.

notes.title: Discharge planning — the bottleneck
notes.content:
Medically fit is not the same as ready to leave. Most delays are social care packages, transport, or a family conversation that has not happened.

None of those are clinical problems and all of them land on the clinical team.

notes.title: Teaching — registrars
notes.content:
Two registrars on the service. Formal teaching Wednesday, informal all week.

The informal is where the learning is and it is the first thing that goes when the census is high.

notes.title: Continuing education — this year
notes.content: Fifty hours required. Twenty-two done. Two conferences booked in off weeks, which is the only way it happens.

notes.title: What an off week is actually for
notes.content:
Recovery, admin, education, and the things that cannot be done on shift.

Colleagues schedule meetings into off weeks because I am 'available', which is technically true and misses the point of a seven-on rota.

notes.title: Antimicrobial stewardship round
notes.content:
Weekly with pharmacy and microbiology. Reviews everyone on broad-spectrum agents.

One of the few multidisciplinary meetings that reliably changes what happens to patients, which is why I protect the time.

notes.title: Mortality and morbidity
notes.content:
Monthly. Case selection is by the clinical governance lead.

The useful ones are the near misses. The ones where the outcome was bad but the care was right are harder and more important.

notes.title: Referral patterns — cardiology
notes.content: Response times vary enormously by who is on. Not a complaint, an observation, and the kind of thing that should be visible and is not.

notes.title: Rota fairness
notes.content:
Someone has to work the December block and the rota rotates it. This year it is me.

Every hospitalist rota in the world has this note and it is never resolved, only rotated.

notes.title: Note quality — my own
notes.content:
Reviewed a sample of my own notes after the audit round. Assessments are good, plans are terse, and the terseness reads as certainty I did not have at the time.

Worth fixing because the next person reads the plan and not the assessment.

notes.title: Service structure — hospitalist rota
notes.content: Seven on, seven off. Days run 07:00 to 19:00 with handover either side. Twelve to sixteen patients on service, higher in winter.

notes.title: Documentation — where the time actually goes
notes.content: Not typing. Finding. Reading yesterday's note, the specialty opinion, and the result that arrived overnight, in three places. The pilot addresses the typing.

notes.title: Teaching — foundation doctors
notes.content: Two attached per rotation. Teaching happens during the round or not at all. On a heavy day it does not happen.

notes.title: Specialty referrals — the friction
notes.content: Bleep, wait, re-explain. The referral system exists and half the specialties do not use it, so I use whichever route that specialty actually answers.

notes.title: Winter pressures — what changes
notes.content: Census up, length of stay up, and the threshold for what counts as safe staffing quietly moves. Nobody says it moved.

notes.title: Why I do not file tickets from the floor
notes.content: Filing a ticket means writing down which patients were open. I report verbally to informatics instead, which means the problem is invisible to anyone reading the ticket queue and I know that.

notes.title: Off-week — what I actually do
notes.content: Sleep for two days. Then the things that need me awake and available: meetings, teaching prep, and anything requiring a conversation longer than four minutes.

notes.title: Continuing education
notes.content: Fifty hours a year. Most of it accrues in the off weeks, which is the only reason it accrues at all.

notes.title: Colleagues' practice — what I will not comment on
notes.content: Asked occasionally, usually informally. Another clinician's decision is theirs and reviewing it is what M&M is for, not a corridor conversation.

notes.title: Junior doctor rota gaps
notes.content: Three unfilled shifts on the next rota. Filled by goodwill and locums. The goodwill is finite and nobody is measuring it.

notes.title: What good looks like in a documentation tool
notes.content: Fewer steps to find. Nothing suggested before I have decided. Nothing written that I did not approve. In that order.
